What are you actually looking at?

That gray layer is what the filter pulled out of one room's air over [six months]: dust, lint and fine particles that stay in the air long after the surfaces look clean. It built up a little every day as the Jaspr drew the room's air through the filter and sent it back out.

New Used

Photo: Jaspr. A new filter next to a used one.

What a used filter shows

  • The unit was pulling air through the filter the whole time.
  • The filter caught particles out of that air, day after day.
  • How much built up over a stated period in one real room.

What it doesn't show

  • Which particles they are. Color and texture aren't a lab test.
  • Whether gases or odors were removed. Particles on a filter say nothing about gases.
  • Anything about health. A dirty filter isn't a measure of how anyone feels.

We'd rather show you the filter and be straight about what it proves than ask you to take a spec sheet on faith.

Clean surfaces don't mean clean air.

Dusting clears what has already settled. A filter catches what's still in the air: particles too small or too light to land where a cloth can reach.

Outdoor air gets in.

Doors, windows and the small gaps every house has let outside air in, along with whatever it's carrying.

Cooking adds to the air.

Searing, frying and toasting put fine particles into the room, even with the range hood on.

Dust gets stirred back up.

Walking, vacuuming, making the bed and air from the vents lift settled dust back into the air you're in.

“My old filter was covered in dust when I pulled it out so after having windows and doors open for summer, I'm glad for a fresh filter now that we're more closed up.”

Diane V., Jaspr owner Needs permission

None of this means a home is dirty. It means the air in it keeps moving, and so does what's in it.

How Jaspr catches it.

Jaspr draws room air in from all the way around its base and pushes it through one large, layered filter before sending it back into the room.

  1. Pre-filter

    Stops lint, hair and larger dust first.

  2. Particle filter

    Catches the fine particles. This is the layer that turns gray in the reveal.

  3. 1 lb of carbon

    There for odors. Its work doesn't show up as color, so we don't use the filter to prove it.

How many do you need?

Jaspr is sized for a room, not a whole house. For most homes Jaspr recommends:

  • One in each bedroom
  • One in the main living or cooking area
  • One in a home office or gym

Open-plan homes and condos often start with one in the main living space. One unit won't cover a whole house, and this page won't pretend it does.

Other owners' filters, in their own homes.

Questions

How many do I need?

Start with the room you spend the most time in, usually the bedroom. Jaspr recommends one per bedroom, one in the main living or cooking area, and one in a home office or gym.

How loud is it?

About 33 dBA at its lowest speed, the speed it runs at most of the time. It speeds up when it detects more in the air, then settles back down.

How do filter changes work?

On the subscription, a new filter ships every six months and you're charged when it ships. Tilt the unit, take off the bottom panel, slide the old filter out and the new one in. It takes about 30 seconds, and there's nothing to vacuum. Watch Jaspr's how-to video.

What if it's not for me?

You have 30 days. If you decide it isn't right for your home, Jaspr buys it back for the full price you paid. Keep the box.
